primitives.name: Triplet Contrastive Loss
primitives.verbatim_quote: We adopt a contrastive learning approach in which an embedding network learns to maximize the distance between representations of players on different teams relative to players on the same team, in a purely unsupervised fashion, without any labelled data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f(x)': 'Embedding function (Euclidean space)', 'x_i^a': 'Anchor player image (team A)', 'x_i^b': 'Positive (same-team) player image', 'x_i^n': 'Negative (different-team) player image', 'm': 'Margin hyperparameter (default 1.0)'}
primitives.assumptions: Requires sufficient intra-class similarity and inter-class dissimilarity in raw embeddings; works best with hard negative mining.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss saturates when inter-class distances exceed intra-class distances plus margin; may fail under extreme class imbalance.

layer2.mapping: Dual to InfoNCE loss in GSI for mutual information maximization; also maps to conformal prediction via empirical risk minimization.
layer2.telemetry: Classification accuracy on held-out validation set

primitives.assumptions: Assumes object separability, sufficient resolution, and stable camera angles; struggles with severe occlusion and motion blur.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance degrades when background clutter exceeds foreground signal; prone to false positives in low-light conditions.

primitives.name: K-Means Clustering
primitives.verbatim_quote: Prior work (e.g., [17, 13]) has framed the problem as a supervised learning task in which labelled data (e.g., bounding boxes with team identifiers) are used to learn a classifier.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'J': 'Clustering objective function (Euclidean distance)', 'w_{ik}': 'Assignment weight (1 if point i belongs to cluster k, else 0)', 'x_i': 'Feature vector for player i', 'c_k': 'Cluster centroid for team k'}
primitives.assumptions: Spherical clusters, equal variance, linearly separable classes; requires careful initialization to avoid local minima.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when clusters have complex shapes or varying densities; sensitivity to outliers reduces robustness.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI posterior estimation via maximum likelihood under Gaussian mixture models; also implements conformal prediction via nearest neighbour search.

primitives.assumptions: Spatial stationarity, continuous player movement, and uniform sampling across the playing field; assumes no systematic bias in player reporting.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is separating two highly overlapping distributions (teams) from minimal labeled data. Triplet loss creates a metric space where same-team points cluster tightly while opposite-team points are pushed apart. This geometric separation enables k-means to recover true assignments even when initial embeddings are random. The key failure mode occurs when color histograms (used for triplet negatives) are identical across teams, causing the loss to collapse. Real-time adaptation relies on incremental updates of cluster centers as new frames arrive, reducing burn-in time. Heat maps are unbiased because they only require correct assignment, not perfect classification confidence.
